provenance.why: M6 (#8) runs offline: cEOS-lab is not installed on this machine and the physical 7050TX-64 is never called from tests. These files are written from documented EOS 4.28 config forms, not captured from a device.
provenance.supersededBy: M12 (#14) captures `show running-config` (format text) under test/fixtures/recordings/ceos-4.28.14M/ and test/fixtures/recordings/7050tx-64-4.28.13.1M/, per docs/STATUS.md §3 and docs/TESTING.md §4.
provenance.parityOracle: pyeapi-oracle.json is generated by scripts/config-chunkify-oracle.py from upstream pyeapi 1.0.4-rc0 (develop 6816d9e) — it records what pyeapi does with these bytes, which is not evidence about EOS.

acl-sections.conf.label: standard and extended `ip access-list` sections, plus a bare ACL with no body
forms: `ip access-list <name>` (extended) with operators, options and a `no statistics per-entry` line
a bare `ip access-list standard EMPTY-STD` section with no body
an `interface Vlan40` section whose name contains `Vlan` so an ACL-only scan cannot borrow it
acl-sections.conf.notes: Hand-authored per this manifest's provenance block: written from the shapes in the Arista 4.28 ACL user guide and pyeapi's own fixture (`pyeapi/test/fixtures/running_config.text:2012-2031`), NOT captured from the 7050TX-64. The wildcard form `permit 10.20.0.0 0.0.255.255` is the standard-ACL spelling pyeapi mis-converts (api/acl.py:178 via netaddr), which is why it is here. Whether this SKU accepts each form is unverified on hardware, M12 (#14) to capture.

banner-eof.conf.label: EOF-terminated multiline banners at indent 0
forms: blank line inside a banner body
banner-eof.conf.notes: pyeapi's own banner regex (api/system.py:97-109 `_parse_banners`, `^…EOF$` under re.M) assumes `EOF` at column 0, which is why the terminator test here is column-0. The chunker compares the EOF line after rstrip only (client.py:743), so an indented EOF never terminates.

banner-indented-not-multiline.conf.label: known limitation: a `banner` opener that is indented is not treated as multiline
forms: indented EOF becoming its own sub-section key
banner-indented-not-multiline.conf.notes: The banner rule is gated on indent 0 and on the raw line starting with 'banner ' (client.py:747). Recorded so M8 (#10) cannot assume nested banners parse as blocks. Not a claim that EOS writes indented banners.

code-unit-control-functions.conf.label: code unit continuation lines under router general / control-functions
forms: policy-script body with braces and arbitrary indentation
code-unit-control-functions.conf.notes: Upstream parity, including the part upstream's own test avoids: because the EOF line is compared after rstrip only, an EOS-indented `      EOF` does not end the swallow, and everything after the code unit — including later sections — lands inside the enclosing section. See MIGRATION.md §5 row 41.

mac-security-profile.conf.label: nested mac-security profile sub-sections (pyeapi's own docstring shape)
mac-security-profile.conf.notes: The `cipher aes256-gcm` sub-line is the shape from client.py:710-712. Whether `profile EMPTY` is legal EOS is a device question (M11 #13 probe), not a parsing one — the parser must not assume a profile always has a body, and the chunker does not.

minimal-with-blank-line.conf.label: a near-default config with a leading blank line
forms: blank line becoming the empty-string section key
minimal-with-blank-line.conf.notes: Records pyeapi's quirk that blank lines are sections with key '' and that repeated `!` markers collapse into a single '!' key whose value is the LAST one. That is why `section('!')` is meaningless and why `getBlock` anchors on `^…$`.

qos-class-policy-map.conf.label: class-map / policy-map with class sub-blocks
forms: a class whose body is one line
qos-class-policy-map.conf.notes: The two `class-map … gold` headers and the `class gold` sub-key share the word `gold`, so this fixture is the regression for an unanchored pattern matching the wrong level.

router-bgp-address-family.conf.label: three levels of nesting: router bgp → vrf → address-family
forms: router bgp with a peer-group neighbor
router-bgp-address-family.conf.notes: The deepest sub-sections come FIRST in the map (client.py:770-771 merge order), and `      address-family ipv4` precedes `   address-family ipv4`, so an unanchored `section('address-family ipv4')` returns the VRF one. Resources must anchor (DR-027/getBlock) — the trap M7 (#9) and M9 (#11) inherit.

switchport-trunk.conf.label: interface blocks with switchport config quoted descriptions and a vlan range
switchport-trunk.conf.notes: Feeds `parseBlock`/`findValue`/`unquote` and the range helpers for M9 (#11). The `allowed vlan` value here is one token — the range string is what EOS writes; nothing in this fixture claims the 7050TX-64 accepts every form.

unhandled-literal-blank-line.conf.label: negative case: blank line inside a block, then an under-length line

unhandled-literal-short-line.conf.label: negative case: body line shallower than the block indent

varp-virtual-router.conf.label: global `ip virtual-router mac-address` plus per-interface `ip virtual-router address` lines
forms: two VLAN interfaces with one and two virtual-router addresses
a VLAN interface with no virtual-router address (empty list)
a routed `interface Ethernet1` carrying a virtual-router address, which pyeapi's `^interface (Vlan\d+)$` scan cannot see
varp-virtual-router.conf.notes: Hand-authored (see the provenance block): these are documented 4.28 forms, modeled on pyeapi's own `test/fixtures/running_config.varp`, not device captures. The `interface Ethernet1` line is deliberate — it pins that both pyeapi (api/varp.py:161) and this module read VARP only from VLAN interfaces, and that the switch may hold VARP state this client does not report. Device behaviour is unverified on hardware, M12 (#14) to capture.

vlan-blocks.conf.label: vlan sections: single, named, ranged and grouped-name forms
vlan-blocks.conf.notes: `vlan 11-13` is the grouped form pyeapi's getall comment mentions (api/vlans.py:186-191). Whether a ranged section carries a body is a device question; the parser must not assume either way.
